title: System timer and watchdog: periodic timer with AXI4 timestamp records, bark interrupt and bite reset request
features: Tick: one every PRESCALE + 1 clocks; COUNT counts ticks.

Timer (TMR_EN): TIMER fires every PERIOD + 1 ticks (the event is the tick at which the timer count is >= PERIOD, so lowering PERIOD ends the current period at the next tick). With TS_EN and TS_WORDS != 0 each timer event writes COUNT (the value in the event's clock) at TS_BASE + 4 * (n mod TS_WORDS); TS_WP counts records, TS_MISSED events that came while a record was being written.
Watchdog (WDT_EN): WDT_COUNT loads WDT_LOAD, counts down one per tick; CMD.kick reloads. At 0: BARK fires and it reloads; at 0 again without a kick wdt_reset goes high until a kick or WDT_EN = 0.

irqs.name: TS_ERR
irqs.desc: a record write got an AXI error response

sequence: Write CTRL.prescale, PERIOD, TS_BASE, TS_WORDS, then CTRL with tmr_en / ts_en.
Watchdog: write WDT_LOAD, set CTRL.wdt_en, write CMD.kick periodically.
notes: m_* is the AXI4 manager port (32-bit address and data, 4-bit ID, no user / QoS); it passes through unchanged. Bursts are INCR, AxSIZE = 2 (4 bytes), 1 to 16 beats, WSTRB = 4'hF, never across a 4 KB boundary; one read and one write burst are outstanding at a time. A read burst is issued only when its data has room, a write burst only when all its data is ready.
wdt_reset (the reset request) drives a pin and reads in WDT_STATE.
